materials: 14 Precisionary Instruments © 2017 PREPARING THE AGAROSE FOR EMBEDDING: We recommend using agarose type-Ib, or low melting point agarose. All tissue specimens should be embedded in agarose. Type-Ib agarose powder can also be purchased through Sigma Aldrich at: http://www.sigmaaldrich.com/catalog/product/sial/a0576?lang=en&region=US The following procedure assumes you are using a 0.5 mg agarose tablet. This table summarizes the buffer volumes to use for agarose tablets. We recommend using a 2.0% or 2.5% agarose solution. Agarose Tablet Chart Solution volume needed to achieve % agarose (mL) Agarose % 1 tablet 2 tablets 3 tablets 1.5% 33 67 100 1.8% 28 56 83 2.0% 25 50 75 2.2% 23 45 68 2.5% 20 40 60 3.0% 17 33 50 3.2% 16 31 47 3.5% 14 29 43 Each tablet contains is 0.5 mg of agarose. Depending on the gel strength you want for slicing, you can add the appropriate amount of water or buffer solution to the glass vial. We recommend adding 20-25 mL of solution to each glass vial containing 1 agarose tablet.

steps.title: Remove transportation stabilization plate
steps.instruction: Unscrew and remove the metal transportation stabilization plate from the back of the vibrating head before first use; keep the plate for future shipments.

steps.title: Prepare and mount cutting blade
steps.instruction: Cut each double‑edged stainless steel blade horizontally to create two single blades (use one); for ceramic blades, remove one from the pack. Squeeze a small amount of super glue onto a petri dish, pipette exactly 5 µL onto the blade holder, trim any curled edges, place the blade onto the holder without touching the edge, and let the glue dry for 3 minutes. Ensure no glue remains on the blade surface. Clean the blade holder with acetone between blade changes. Replace blades after 3‑5 soft samples or 1‑2 fibrous samples; ceramic blades last 2‑3 months.

steps.title: Align blade holder for sectioning
steps.instruction: Soak the blade holder in an acetone bath for 5 minutes, then wipe residual glue with a paper towel. Place the specimen syringe tube in the hole of the plastic base with the stopper up and the tapered end facing the buffer tank; push it forward until the stopper contacts the base. Lay a white sheet of paper on the buffer tank to see the gap and minimize the gap between blade holder and tube opening. Rotate the blade holder away from the tube, press the start button, then press stop when the sliding blade assembly has moved down past two‑thirds of the tube opening. Rotate the holder toward the tube, adjust the blade edge to be very close but not touching the tube outlet, and tighten the set screw without rotating the holder. Remove the specimen syringe for embedding.

steps.title: Prepare low‑melting agarose solution
steps.instruction: Swirl the agarose tablet in a glass vial for 2 minutes to dissolve. Microwave the solution in 10‑second bursts, shaking between bursts, until it becomes clear. Cool the clear solution for 5 minutes in a 32 °C water bath. Use the low‑transition temperature agarose tablets supplied in the starter kit.

steps.title: Chill syringe chilling block
steps.instruction: Place the syringe chilling block in an ice‑water bath or freezer; cool for at least 15 minutes (or 10 minutes at –20 °C) before use.

steps.title: Glue tissue to specimen tube base
steps.instruction: Trim the tissue so it fits inside the specimen tube. Squeeze a small amount of super glue onto the tube base, then use forceps to position and adhere the tissue to the base.

steps.title: Embed tissue in agarose
steps.instruction: Place the embedding cap on the top of the specimen tube. Pipette enough molten agarose to fully cover the tissue, gently tap the cap to release air bubbles, then withdraw the syringe tube downward so the tissue enters the tube. Remove the cap.

steps.title: Solidify agarose
steps.instruction: Position the pre‑chilled syringe chilling block over the specimen tube; chill for less than 1 minute (maximum 1.5 minutes) until the agarose solidifies.

steps.title: Set up Compresstome and load specimen
steps.instruction: Connect the power cable to the control box and the control box to the VF‑300‑0Z microtome; tighten both connector screws. Turn the power on. Insert the specimen syringe tube into the buffer tray, pushing it as far as possible with the tapered end first; the stopper knob will prevent the tube from sliding completely. (Blade should already be aligned.)

steps.title: Adjust slicing parameters and cut sections
steps.instruction: Set the desired slice thickness, sectioning speed, and oscillation frequency, then run the slicer to obtain sections.

steps.title: Clean buffer tray and perform post‑run cleanup
steps.instruction: Empty the buffer tank. Clean the buffer tray with 70 % ethanol or 10 % bleach (do not use acetone). Loosen the thumbscrew and push the step‑motor drive away.

steps.title: Clean specimen tube, plunger, and blade holder
steps.instruction: Remove the specimen syringe from the plastic base. Detach the plunger, scrape residual glue from its front end, and clean the plunger and interior of the tube with acetone swabs or a soft brush. Remove the razor blade from the holder. Dip the blade holder into an acetone bath for 5 minutes, then wipe away any remaining glue with a paper towel.

description: 3 Precisionary Instruments © 2017 INTRODUCTION Congratulations on your purchase of a Compresstome® VF-300-0Z from Precisionary Instruments! The VF-300-0Z tissue slicer model is the flagship product in the Compresstome® slicer family with patented Auto Zero-Z® technology. The VF-300-0Z is fully automated to section both fixed and live tissues with a thickness range of 4 µm to 1000 µm with an adjustable precision of 1 µm. The Compresstome® VF-300-0Z excels at sectioning slices used for: ● Electrophysiology ● Immunohistochemistry ● Organotypic culture slices ● Precision cut tissue slices ● Sectioning of mature or older brain tissues ● And much more! At Precisionary Instruments, we are thrilled to help you get started with the new vibrating microtome, and we take great pride in quality customer service. Please read the following manual to help you get started with the Compresstome® VF-300-0Z.
